title: Understanding MAE
text: The Mean Absolute Error (MAE) is calculated as the average of the absolute differences between the predicted values and the actual values. It is given by the formula: MAE=sum{i\=1}{N}{abs(y_i-\hat{y})}/N, where $$y_i$$ is the actual value and \hat{y} is the predicted value.

title: Constant Model
text: In a constant model, the predicted value \hat{y} is the same for all observations. This means $$\hat{y}=\theta_0$$ for every data point.

title: Minimizing MAE with a Constant Model
text: To minimize the MAE in a constant model, $$\theta_0$$ should be chosen such that the sum of the absolute differences between $$\theta_0$$ and the actual values is minimized.

title: Finding the Optimal $$\theta_0$$
text: The value of $$\theta_0$$ that minimizes the MAE is the median of the actual values. This is because the median minimizes the sum of absolute deviations.
